music.prompt: Warm, hopeful, gentle instrumental background music for a nonprofit documentary-style product demo with a narrator. Major key, uplifting but calm. Soft felt piano playing a simple optimistic melody, warm string pads, light acoustic guitar picking, very soft brushed percussion, round warm bass. 84 BPM. Even, steady energy from start to finish, no build-ups, no drops, no solos, no vocals, no choir, no humming. Leave space in the midrange for a voice. Gentle fade-out ending.

scenes.narration: This is Tidepath Family Alliance, a made-up Miami nonprofit that mentors kids and supports their families. It has seven staff jobs. Here, one person, Alex, does all of them. The hackathon gave six real problems from South Florida nonprofits. We solve each one inside Roomcord.

captions: This is *Tidepath Family Alliance*, a made-up Miami nonprofit that mentors kids and supports their families.

The hackathon gave *six real problems* from South Florida nonprofits.
We solve each one inside *Roomcord*.

scenes.narration: Alex works in Roomcord, a workspace where people and AI agents work side by side. Roomcord hosts the agents. They run on a custom Codex engine, and you configure them just by talking to them. Every job has its own room: programs, volunteers, workshops, fundraising, counseling and grants. Each room has an agent that does that one job. Staff build powerful automations on these agents right inside Roomcord, with no hard integration choices. Roomcord takes in and produces all kinds of files and media, so agents get the full context.

scenes.narration: Problem five: volunteer updates get lost in group chats, and urgent needs reach staff too late. Maria, a volunteer mentor, opens Tidepath’s public website on her phone. In one minute she reports an hour with Kevin, and an urgent need: Kevin's school laptop broke. Her check-in lands in the Volunteers room. The volunteer agent logs the hour once, so nothing is counted twice, and flags the laptop as urgent. Alex asks the Director agent to pass the need to the Programs team. It arrives there the same day, addressed to Alex. Every check-in also goes into one shared record that all the agents read.

scenes.narration: Problem one: staff type the same details again and again, follow-ups are missed, and the quarterly report takes days. In Programs and mentoring, Alex asks who needs a call this week. The agent checks attendance and mentor meetings. It has weeks of history here, from sign-ups, attendance sheets and volunteer check-ins. Kevin missed three sessions, and Jaylen hasn't met his mentor in weeks. It drafts a message to Kevin's mother, marked draft, not sent. Nothing goes out until a person approves it.

Kevin's record now holds his sign-up, his attendance, Maria's visit and the laptop request. The more the team uses the rooms, the more each record holds, and the more each agent can do.

scenes.narration: The second half of problem two: donors who quietly stop giving. In Fundraising, the agent knows each donor's usual giving pattern. It builds that pattern from each donor's past gifts, so every new gift makes its check sharper. Two regular donors are late. One monthly gift failed yesterday. The agent flags it the next morning, so staff can fix it before the donor is lost.
